dedupe_keys.name: solar and wind energy on port buildings at alexandria port egypt measured and simulated energy plan espr 2023

description: A study by engineers at the Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport and Alexandria University, published in Environmental Science and Pollution Research in 2023, of supplying port buildings at Alexandria, a Mediterranean port, with solar and wind power. Coverage: buildings in one Egyptian port. Methods: an onsite weather station and installed solar arrays gave measured data; DesignBuilder simulated the solar output and was validated against the site; ANSYS Fluent simulated H-Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbines (0.8 m rotors with NACA0018 blades) on the buildings; a Pareto optimality analysis combined both into an energy management plan. Outcome: solar panels met the buildings' demand, the simulated turbines showed good power coefficients for future use, and renewable energy could cover the buildings' consumption. Format and access: open article on PubMed Central; measured data are available from the corresponding author on request. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: small building-scale systems, not port operations such as cranes or shore power. Useful for optimisation and capacity planning of renewable supply at ports. It relates to the WindEurope offshore wind ports vision and the CLIA shore power map in the catalogue.
